SHANGHAI, February 17th 1944.
U 352
2 44
Re Miss Zlotnicki.
Miss A. Zlotnicki is engaged to marry. Her fiance is
Mr. Alexander Menczer, who is manufacturing leather-goods. He has a very good
reputation and he is rather well off. He is working together with his brother
and both are very industrious. Mr. Mencuer bought on the 14th of February
a hous situated in Paoting Road and let it get repaired. The marriage shall
take place in about three months.

关于兹洛特尼茨基小姐 (Miss Zlotnicki)。
兹洛特尼茨基小姐 (A. Zlotnicki) 已订婚。她的未婚夫是
亚历山大·门策尔先生 (Mr. Alexander Menczer)，从事皮革制品制造。他声誉
极佳，且相当富裕。他与兄弟共同工作，两人都非常勤奋。门策尔先生 (Mr. Mencuer) 于2月14日
购买了一处位于保定路 (Paoting Road) 的房屋，并进行了修缮。婚礼预计
在大约三个月后举行。

pages.en:
To the
First Police Bureau, Special Branch
Shanghai.

Sir,

I beg to report re A. Zlotnicki as follows:

The financial circumstances of the family are unchanged.
The only one person in the family who is earning something
is the daughter, Miss Alice. She is crossing neckties and
gets wages 27.50 $ each piece. She is able to make three pieces a
week at most. Of course she has the idea to make these neckties
on her own account but for the time being she is unable to do so
owing to the difficulty of getting the raw-material and besides
nobody of the whole family has a special pass which should allow
them to leave the designated area.

In the last time the family sold one opera-glass/300.--$/one pair
of nearly new shoes of Mr. 2./500.-- /one fur for gentlemen/2200/
and one fruit-set/1700.--./The family has still other articles of
value ready for sale amongst them one complete set of knife fork
and spoon made of silver and furthermore the family has different
articles of great value as jewellery so they can live a long time
on selling those goods. I am keeping continuing to observe.

Your most obedient servant

先生：

谨就 A. 兹洛特尼茨基 (A. Zlotnicki) 一事报告如下：

该家庭的经济状况未变。
家中唯一有收入的人
是其女儿，爱丽丝小姐 (Miss Alice)。她从事领带穿线工作，
每件工资为27.50美元。她每周最多
能制作三件。当然，她有意自行经营
这项领带业务，但目前由于难以获得原材料，加之
全家无人持有允许离开指定区域的特别通行证，故无法实现。

近期，该家庭出售了一件歌剧望远镜/300.--美元/一双
近乎全新的男士皮鞋/500.--美元/一件男士皮草/2200美元/
以及一套水果餐具/1700.--美元/。家庭中仍有其他贵重物品
待售，其中包括一套完整的银制刀叉勺，此外该家庭还拥有
珠宝等不同高价值物品，因此靠变卖这些物品可以维持
相当长一段时间的生活。我将继续保持观察。

您最顺从的仆人

（印：FILE）

re: A. Zlotnicki.

Sir,

I beg to report as follows:

In former times the father N.Zlotnicki has been employed
at the Committee for the Assistance of Central European
Refugees and later on he became manager of the Yuenchang
Bakery at Chusan Rd. with a monthly salary of $ 1.000.--.

Shortly before his daughter has been arrested he changed
his position and became manager of the Dalny Bakery under
the same conditions. After the arrest of his daughter he
became mopish and neglected his business. The Bakery engaged
a substitute and Mr.Zlotnicki lost his job.

As far as it is known the family always lived in good
conditions and probably brought a good deal of valuables
to Shanghai. Before they had also a shop in Wayside Rd.
Miss Alice Zlotnicki had been employed at an Indian Company
(41 Kiukiang Rd.) for a long time. Since the owners very
often stayed in India she was independent in carrying out
business of the company. From this time comes her aquaintance
with Japanese and Indian gentlemen for a Japanese company
shared the office with the employers of Miss Zlotnicki.
Several times Miss Zlotnicki has been invited by correspon-
dents of the company. Since she has been released she stays
mostly at home and has no occupation. The family lives now
under rather bad conditions.

FILE

Your most obedient servant
（签名）

关于：A. 兹洛特尼茨基 (A. Zlotnicki)。

先生：

谨报告如下：

父亲 N. 兹洛特尼茨基 (N.Zlotnicki) 过去曾受雇于
中欧难民援助委员会，后来成为中山路 (Chusan Rd.) 元昌面包店 (Yuenchang Bakery) 的经理，月薪为1,000美元。

在其女儿被捕前不久，他更换了职位，在同等条件下
成为达尔尼面包店 (Dalny Bakery) 的经理。女儿被捕后，
他变得郁郁寡欢，疏于业务。面包店雇佣了替代人员，
兹洛特尼茨基先生 (Mr.Zlotnicki) 因此失业。

据所知，该家庭一直生活优渥，可能携带了大量贵重物品
来到上海。此前他们在韦思德路 (Wayside Rd.) 还拥有一家店铺。
爱丽丝·兹洛特尼茨基小姐 (Miss Alice Zlotnicki) 曾在一家印度公司
（九江路41号）长期任职。由于雇主经常
待在印度，她在处理公司业务方面拥有自主权。也正因如此，
她与日本和印度绅士结识，因为一家日本公司与
兹洛特尼茨基小姐的雇主共用办公室。兹洛特尼茨基小姐
曾多次受到该公司通信员的邀请。自获释以来，她主要
待在家中，无职业。该家庭目前生活条件
相当恶劣。

档案 (FILE)

您最顺从的仆人
（签名）
